definitions.gloss: combustible material; burnable trash; flammable item
definitions.explanation: Materials that can burn. In everyday Japanese life, most commonly refers to burnable garbage in the context of waste sorting.

examples.japanese: {可燃物|かねんぶつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{火曜日|かようび}→火曜日：00640_kayoubi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|だ}して→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please put out burnable trash on Tuesdays.

examples.japanese: ⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{可燃物|かねんぶつ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{不燃物|ふねんぶつ}→不燃物：19230_funenbutsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分|わ}け→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: You have to separate garbage into burnable and non-burnable items.

examples.japanese: ⟦{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}して→引っ越す：01171_hikkosu⟧きた⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、{可燃物|かねんぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{収集日|しゅうしゅうび}→収集日：17710_shuushuubi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧わからない。
examples.english: I just moved in and don't know the burnable trash collection day yet.

notes:
USAGE:
Essential vocabulary for daily life in Japan, where garbage separation is strictly enforced. {可燃物|かねんぶつ} (also called ⟦{可燃|かねん}→可燃：26077_kanen⟧⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧ or ⟦{燃|も}えるゴミ→燃えるゴミ：17105_moerugomi⟧) includes paper, food scraps, and some plastics. Each municipality has specific rules.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {可燃物|かねんぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧ (burnable trash day)
- {可燃物|かねんぶつ}⟦{収集|しゅうしゅう}→収集：11829_shuushuu⟧ (burnable trash collection)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{不燃物|ふねんぶつ}→不燃物：19230_funenbutsu⟧: non-burnable trash — glass, metals, ceramics
- ⟦{燃|も}えるゴミ→燃えるゴミ：17105_moerugomi⟧: burnable garbage — casual, everyday equivalent
- ⟦{資源|しげん}→資源：03167_shigen⟧⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧: recyclable waste — a separate category
